0.0.n: Used to acknowledge the audience and begin the wrap-up.

0.2.n: Combines with わけで to introduce a conclusion or transition.

0.3.n: In というわけで, this helps connect the wrap-up to what came before.

0.4.n: Connects というわけ to what follows, completing the transition phrase.

0.5.n: Here ですね is a polite conversational filler rather than a separate statement.

0.6.n: Softens the transition and keeps the audience engaged.

0.9.n: A proper name used here as the game's title; 城 means castle.

0.11.n: Adds politeness as the speaker identifies the game title.

0.12.n: Invites the audience to follow along with the title being mentioned.

1.0.n: A conversational filler that eases into the explanation.

1.1.n: Combines 旧, former, 輸入, import, and 名, name, to describe the game's earlier title.

1.2.n: Marks the former imported title as the topic.

1.3.n: Here ですね fills a pause politely before the actual title.

1.4.n: Softens the pause while the speaker continues the sentence.

1.7.n: Describes Ludwig within the game's former Japanese title.

1.8.n: A personal name referring here to King Ludwig II of Bavaria.

1.9.n: Links Ludwig to his castle or castles.

1.10.n: Japanese does not mark singular or plural here; the supplied English game title uses the plural.

1.12.n: Politely finishes the identification of the former title.

1.13.n: Adds a friendly, audience-directed tone to the statement.

2.0.n: Introduces the final summary in a relaxed conversational tone.

2.1.n: Refers back to the game just named, using a polite alternative to これ.

2.2.n: Connects this game to its Japanese edition, despite the intervening filler ですね.

2.3.n: Part of the filler ですね, inserted between の and 日本語版.

2.4.n: Softens the inserted pause without changing the sentence's main structure.

2.6.n: Combines 日本語, Japanese language, with 版, edition.

2.7.n: Marks the Japanese edition as what the speaker presented.

2.8.n: The お-prefixed stem of 届ける combines with しました to politely describe presenting something to viewers.

2.9.n: Polite past form of する; with お届け, it means the speaker presented the game.

3.0.n: Part of the English channel name The Game Gallery.

3.2.n: Part of the English channel name The Game Gallery, not a separate Japanese word.

3.4.n: Completes the English channel name The Game Gallery.

3.5.n: An English-derived word identifying the named video channel.

3.6.n: Links the presenter to the channel they belong to.

3.7.n: The name portion of the presenter's handle Haru99.

3.8.n: The numeric portion of the presenter's handle Haru99.

3.9.n: The first part of でした, the polite past form of です.

3.10.n: Completes でした; the past form is used here for a closing self-identification.

0.lit: Alright, that being so, it is Neuschwanstein Castle, you know.
0.tip: というわけで signals a transition or wrap-up, much like so or with that.

1.lit: Well, as for the former imported title, it is Mad King Ludwig's Castles, you know.
1.tip: The first ですね is just a polite filler between the topic and the title.

2.lit: Well, this one's, you see, Japanese edition, I presented.
2.tip: Ignore the inserted ですね to see the core phrase こちらの日本語版, this game's Japanese edition.

3.lit: It was Haru99 of The Game Gallery channel.
3.tip: Ending with a name plus でした is a common sign-off, like this has been Haru99.
